steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) vs. RNA (ribonucleic acid):

1. Sugar  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen)  
   • RNA: ribose  

2. Strands  
   • DNA: usually double-stranded helix  
   • RNA: usually single-stranded  

3. Bases  
   • DNA: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), guanine (G)  
   • RNA: A, uracil (U) instead of T, C, G  

4. Function  
   • DNA: long-term genetic storage in nucleus (and mitochondria)  
   • RNA: messenger (mRNA), transfer (tRNA), ribosomal (rRNA) and regulatory roles in protein synthesis and gene regulation  

5. Stability  
   • DNA: more chemically stable (suitable for permanent storage)  
   • RNA: less stable, more transient (suited to quick roles)
